hooks.command: input=$(cat); sid=$(jq -r '.session_id' <<<"$input"); cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command' <<<"$input"); if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE -- '-D[= ]warnings|--deny[= ]warnings'; then mkdir -p /tmp/claude-quality-clean && touch "/tmp/claude-quality-clean/$sid.clippy"; fi

input=$(cat); sid=$(jq -r '.session_id' <<<"$input"); cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command' <<<"$input"); if echo "$cmd" | grep -q -- '-l rust' && echo "$cmd" | grep -q 'crates'; then mkdir -p /tmp/claude-quality-clean && touch "/tmp/claude-quality-clean/$sid.lizard"; fi

sid=$(jq -r '.session_id'); missing=''; [ -f "/tmp/claude-quality-clean/$sid.clippy" ] || missing="clippy"; [ -f "/tmp/claude-quality-clean/$sid.lizard" ] || missing="$missing lizard"; if [ -z "$missing" ]; then echo '{}'; else echo "{\"hookSpecificOutput\":{\"hookEventName\":\"PreToolUse\",\"permissionDecision\":\"ask\",\"permissionDecisionReason\":\"Run 'just quality' (clippy + lizard) and fix the underlying issue behind anything it flags before committing - missing:$missing. Codacy cannot analyze Rust in this flatpak environment, so these are the real local gates; do not restructure code just to dodge a specific rule's counting behavior, see CLAUDE.md.\"}}"; fi
